notes:
Overview
- Fast-growing self-serve SaaS customer. Primary product is an AI knowledge base / doc-search experience for enterprise teams; heavy embeddings + chat summarization.
- Flagged by Finance/Telemetry anomaly monitoring due to spend spike + invoice vs console delta reports (customer-reported ~5–7% on a few days). Usage is real, but they’re sensitive to any unexplained variance.

Firmographics / stack
- HQ: US (West). Cloud: AWS.
- Current integration: Redwood Hosted API via Python + TypeScript services; streaming enabled for chat; embeddings batch jobs nightly.
- Workload pattern: weekdays heavy interactive chat; nights heavy embeddings (index refresh + incremental ingestion).

Product usage (what they run)
- Endpoints: /chat.completions (streaming), /embeddings, occasional /rerank for search results.
- Implementation notes from SE: they retry aggressively (client + gateway) on 429/5xx; also have their own request fan-out for multi-doc summarization.
- Latency: interactive SLO ~1.5–2.5s TTFB on streaming; embeddings throughput prioritized over p95 latency.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high; CFO asked for predictable monthly bill; wants “why did we get charged for retries/disconnects?” answered plainly.

Why they’re on the anomaly watchlist
- Jan/early Feb: spend spikes coincident with a product launch + ingestion backfill. Alerts fired for: (a) day-over-day token increase >80%, (b) mismatch between billing-ready aggregates vs console totals.
- Customer complaint theme: “console says X tokens, invoice shows X * 1.06; we need to explain to our finance team.”
- Internal hypothesis at the time: mix of streaming disconnect accounting + retry double counting on one endpoint. Account was used as a ‘canary’ for monitoring because they have high request volume and clear internal observability (they log request_id).

Support / escalations
- SUP-3112: "Invoice tokens higher than console by ~6%" (hosted). Investigation referenced: time zone boundaries (console local vs invoice UTC), per-request rounding artifacts in older aggregation, and streaming partials. Resolved with explanation + offered one-time courtesy credit pending platform fix verification.
- SUP-3160: streaming disconnects perceived as overbilling. Customer had clients dropping websockets during peak traffic. They asked: "are we billed for tokens generated after disconnect?" Support response: should not bill post-disconnect; Engineering shipped fix + backfill plan; customer asked to confirm on next invoice cycle.

Recent activity timeline
- 2026-02-04: Support triage reopened after customer compared console export vs draft invoice totals; asked for breakdown by model + day.
- 2026-02-06: SE (Mei) met with their lead engineer; got sample of ~200 request_ids across chat streaming + retries; agreed to run reconciliation on Redwood side.
- 2026-02-11: Internal note from Telemetry: suspected retry accounting issue on one route (tokens counted on failed attempt + successful retry). Waiting on request_outcome dimension rollout to separate billed vs non-billed.
- 2026-02-14: Customer asked whether pricing experiment credits stack with standard discount codes in self-serve (forwarded to Sales Ops for approved talk track).
- 2026-02-19: CSM (Rachel) check-in: customer wants a 1-pager they can send to Finance: definitions of input/output tokens, cached tokens, streaming partials, retries, rounding. They are open to committing if measurement is “audit-friendly.”

Key requirements / objections (verbatim-ish)
- "We can live with small differences day-to-day, but we need a single source of truth and a way to audit from request_id -> billed units." 
- "We need clarity on what happens when our clients disconnect mid-stream, and when we retry. Are we paying twice?" 
- "If we move from self-serve to a commit, we need predictable burn-down and no surprises from aggregation changes." 

Success plan / next steps
- Provide customer-facing explanation (internal draft first) aligning: console vs invoice time window (UTC), rounding policy (aggregate-level), retry treatment (billed only on successful outcomes; failed attempts excluded once request_outcome is live), and streaming disconnect behavior (no tokens after disconnect; partial tokens up to disconnect billed).
- Run reconciliation using their request_id sample after next invoice preview; target: deltas within 0.5% when aligned by aggregation window + filters.
- If stable for 2 weeks, propose moving them to a higher tier (more included credits + lower overage) rather than exploring Dedicated; they explicitly do not want VPC/on-prem right now.

Internal-only notes
- Keep on meter anomaly monitoring list until daily reconciliation job shows stable deltas and alerts are suppressed during backfills.
- Loop in Dev Patel on any further disputes; Finance wants consistent refund/credit approvals (no ad-hoc promises).
